cases.name: Nellie Whitstine Rousseau
cases.about: Her obituary said, "In her younger years Nellie played softball with her sisters, sister-in-laws, and other friends. Their teams were, Roadrunners and OK Lakerettes. When she moved to Florida, she and Charlie played tennis competitively throughout the state. Professionally, she worked at Red River Egg Company, retail accounting in Florida, and Grant Parish Police Jury. Nellie was a loving sister. Being third from the oldest, she was a second mom to those younger than her. She was always there with support and love. She selflessly helped mom raise and nurture the younger siblings. If the younger ones needed a bottle, a diaper changed or just an old-fashioned butt whipping, she offered as needed. As a wife, Nellie was a steadfast partner. Throughout their journey together, she stood by Charlie offering comfort in times of sorrow and celebrating joy in times of triumph. Her life was defined by her unconditional love for her children and grandchildren whom she nurtured with boundless patience. Her home was a sanctuary of warmth and comfort, where her children found solace and guidance in her embrace. Nellie's devotion to her family extended beyond her children; she was a source of support to all who knew her. Her love for her parents, siblings, children, and grandchildren can never be questioned. She never wavered from helping anyone that needed her. That's the "Sissy" that will forever live in our memories. Her legacy as a loving sister, wife, mother, and friend will forever be cherished and remembered, a testament to the profound impact she had on those fortunate enough to have her in their lives. She will be missed and loved forever."
